info.title: RosteredAI Tenant Integrations API
info.description:
The integration API for organisations on RosteredAI. Read and update your organisation, locations, staff,
qualifications, leave, pay conditions, rosters, agency shifts, timesheets, forms and tasks, and stay in sync through
signed webhooks.

## Authentication
OAuth 2.0 **client credentials**. Create a credential in **Settings › Integrations** (the client secret is shown once) and
choose what it may do: each scope there lists the exact calls it unlocks. Then call `POST /user/api/integrations/token`
(form-encoded, or with the id and secret as HTTP Basic) to exchange your `client_id` and `client_secret` for a bearer
token, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every other call. Rotating or revoking a credential, or your
organisation being deactivated, stops every token it issued within about a minute. A token carries only the scopes your
plan includes: after a plan change, any scope the new plan leaves out stops working within about a minute, and the next
token no longer carries it. Use the **Authorize** button above to try calls on this page.

## Scopes
Every operation lists the scopes that let a token call it, any one of which is enough. Most reads accept the area's `.read`
or `.write` scope; writes need `.write`; approvals need `leave.approve` or `timesheets.approve`; publishing needs
`rosters.publish`. Bank, super and tax reads and the staff export need `staff.finance.read`, and `staff.finance.write`
alone is refused. A call without a matching scope is refused with `403`.

### Fields with their own scope
Some sensitive fields need a scope of their own, on top of the one that opens the call. Without it the call still succeeds,
and those fields come back null (a few text fields come back blank, and a few ids as the all-zero id):
- `staff.personal.read`: staff date of birth, contact details, address, profile picture and documents.
- `staff.finance.read`: tax file number, payroll id and time-clock passcode on staff records.
- `pay_conditions.read`: pay rates, costs and amounts on staff, roster and timesheet reads.
- `forms.responses.read`: the answers and review comments on form submissions. It opens no call by itself.

The matching `.write` scope does not unlock these. Searching or sorting by a field you cannot read is ignored.
Operations say which fields this affects.

## Conventions
- Paths are shown as you call them on this host; each starts with the area of RosteredAI that answers it.
- Most responses use the envelope `{ "data": …, "message": "…" }`. The token endpoint answers in the OAuth 2.0 shape, and
  file downloads return the file.
- Bodies are **camelCase JSON** unless an operation says multipart/form-data. Ids are GUIDs; dates are ISO-8601.
- **Shift and attendance times are the location's wall clock**, sent with no offset; they are not UTC. Do not add an offset
  or convert them. `timeZone`, where a record has it, names the zone they belong to. A null `timeZone` means that
  location has no zone set; set one with *Set a location's opening hours and time zone*. Fields ending in `Utc` are UTC.
- Your organisation comes from your token. Where a request carries a tenant id, it must be your own (or is replaced by
  it, where the operation says so). Send only your own staff, location, area, shift and timesheet ids.
- Fields naming who made a change are ignored. Changes to main records are recorded against your credential. Not every
  write is covered, and the API doesn't return this.
- A `pageSize` above 200 is lowered to 200 without an error. Very large sizes (above 10000, or above 500 for areas) are
  still refused with `400`, except on tags.
- This version has no external ids, no idempotency keys, no changed-since reads and no record versions. Retrying a create
  that may have succeeded can create a duplicate, so read before you retry. Not every change raises a webhook, so re-read
  periodically rather than relying on events alone.

## Status codes
| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `200` / `201` | Success. |
| `400` | The request was missing something or failed validation; `message` says what. |
| `401` | The bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or was revoked or rotated. |
| `403` | Your token lacks the required scope, or the request names another organisation. |
| `404` | The item does not exist, or is not yours. |
| `409` | Blocked by a dependency, a duplicate or a plan limit. |
| `500` | Unexpected server error; `message` carries a reference to quote to support. |
| `503` | A dependency is briefly unavailable; try again shortly. |

Another organisation's data is never returned, but the answer depends on the call: `404`, `403`, `400`, or `200` with
empty or null `data`. Treat all of them as "not yours".

The token endpoint follows OAuth 2.0 instead and returns `{ error, error_description }` with `400` or `401`. It is the only
call that is rate limited today, so it is the only one that can answer `429`.

## Webhooks
Register endpoints, choose events, send tests and read the delivery log under `/user/api/integrations/webhooks/...`.
Every event we can send is documented as a **callback** on *Register or update a webhook endpoint*, with its `data`.
Each delivery is a POST of `{ eventId, eventType, occurredAt, data }`.

### Verifying a delivery
Each endpoint has its own signing secret (`whsec_…`), shown once when the endpoint is created or its secret rotated.
Every delivery carries `X-RosteredAI-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, plus `X-RosteredAI-Event-Id`,
`X-RosteredAI-Delivery-Id` (unique per attempt), `X-RosteredAI-Event-Type` and `X-RosteredAI-Api-Version`.
1. Read the **raw** request body before parsing it.
2. Split the header on `,` into `t` and `v1`.
3. Compute HMAC-SHA256 with your endpoint's secret over `t + "." + rawBody`, as lowercase hex.
4. Compare it with `v1` in constant time; reject the delivery if they differ.
5. Reject a `t` more than a few minutes old, so a captured delivery cannot be replayed to you.
6. Deduplicate on `eventId`: a retry or a replay carries the same id.
7. Answer `2xx` quickly and do the work afterwards.

### Retries
A delivery is tried up to **8 times**: straight away, then 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours, 12 hours
and 24 hours after the previous attempt (about 43 hours in all), then it stops. `410 Gone` stops retries at once, and
three in a row suspend the endpoint. An endpoint whose deliveries have all failed for 24 hours is disabled at its next
failure, and your integration admins are emailed; events raised while it is off are not sent to it later. A stopped
delivery from the last 30 days can be replayed from the delivery log.

> Replace the server `host` variable with the production (or sandbox) address your RosteredAI contact provides.

post.summary: Set a location's opening hours and time zone
post.description:
Sets the opening hours and time zone of one of your locations, replacing whatever it had. This is how a location gets a time zone through the API. `data` is the location id.

Send the zone as `timeZoneName`, an IANA name such as `Australia/Sydney`, or as the lookup id in `timeZone`; one of the two is required, and they must agree when both are sent. The zone is stored with the hours, so at least one opening time is needed. A missing or unsupported zone, or a schedule with no opening time, a wrong day or a range not running forward within the day, answers 400. A location of another organisation answers 403, and one that does not exist answers 404. `isUpdate`, `createdBy` and `modifiedBy` are ignored.

**Required scope:** `locations.write`

See **Responses** below for the status codes this operation can return.

timeZoneName.description: IANA zone name. Required unless `timeZone` is sent.

timeZone.description: The zone's lookup id, as the read returns it. Required unless `timeZoneName` is sent.

dailyOperatingHours.description: The days with hours. At least one opening time overall.

hasSplitHours.description: True when the day has more than one range.

from.description: Opening time, HH:mm:ss, the location's wall clock.

to.description: Closing time, HH:mm:ss, later the same day.

post.description:
Creates a location when `tenantLocationId` is empty or left out, or updates one of yours when it is set. `data` is the location id. The contact person is stored on the location as plain details: your integration never creates or links a login account for them. A refused save answers with `data` null: 409 when a new location would pass your plan's location limit, when the name is already used in your organisation, or when the contact person's details are already in use; 400 when nothing could be stored. `tenantId` must be your own organisation id, and an edited location must be yours, or the call answers 404. An edit saves every other field as sent, so send the whole location: a field left out is cleared. `status` and `tagsWithColor` apply on create only and are kept as stored on an edit.

A location has no time zone until you set one with "Set a location's opening hours and time zone".

**Required scope:** `locations.write`

See **Responses** below for the status codes this operation can return.

post.description:
Creates an area when `tenantAreaId` is empty or left out, or updates one of yours when it is set. `data` is the area id.

Your integration never changes who works in the area: the area's staff and managers are kept as stored. The location, and an edited area, must belong to your organisation, or the call answers 404. Area names must be unique within the location; a duplicate answers 409. An edit saves the fields as sent, so send the whole area: a text field left out is cleared, and `status` left out is 0 (Inactive).

**Required scope:** `locations.write`

See **Responses** below for the status codes this operation can return.

Each row also carries the staff member's payroll id and time-clock passcode, so treat the response as sensitive.

Staff who have not set a password yet are included. Date of birth, contact details, address and documents need `staff.personal.read`; payroll id and time-clock passcode need `staff.finance.read`; pay rate fields need `pay_conditions.read`. Without the scope the field is null or blank. Without `staff.personal.read`, searching by email or mobile and sorting by mobile are ignored.
